key_insight: Twisted SrTiO3 membranes exhibit a reconstructed moiré interface with polar distortions, modulated Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance.
engineering_relevance: Controlling oxide interface termination and twist could enable tunable electrical behavior, although this study does not demonstrate AI methods or solar-cell applications.
method: Stack atomically flat, twisted SrTiO3 membranes.
Establish a predominantly SrO–TiO2 interfacial configuration.
Directly visualize buried-interface reconstruction and probe electrical signatures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports moiré-periodic reconstruction distinct from rigid stacking, head-to-head-like polar distortions, modulated Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance, without quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Contamination, roughness, and mixed surface terminations can obscure interfacial structures and complicate reproducible fabrication.
paper_title: Moiré reconstruction at a twisted SrTiO3 interface
